mainTopic: Leaders and their generations, then the opening of פרק השג יד: whose wealth decides the amount in ערכין and in a מצורע's offerings.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of a statement from the previous page: a person who goes without suffering has a calamity waiting for him. Next, רבי אליעזר הגדול teaches that even אברהם, יצחק and יעקב could not have stood up to strict judgment. Then רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבנן argue over whether a generation follows its leader or the leader follows his generation. The גמרא first suggests the argument is about goodness, but rejects that from יהויקים and צדקיה, whose generations did not match them. It concludes that the argument is about harshness and gentleness. After the הדרן for פרק יש בערכין, a new משנה teaches that affordability (השג יד) in ערכין follows the one who vows. With a מצורע's offerings, it follows the מצורע instead, and רבי adds a case where ערכין works the same way. The גמרא explains the משנה's wording and its source in the פסוק. It then works through who may bring a poor מצורע's offering, ending with a challenge to רבי יצחק's answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A calamity awaits him
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of a statement from the previous page: such a person has trouble waiting for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A calamity awaits him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous page. The statement says that this person has trouble waiting for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to the previous discussion about suffering, not to anything new. It is the last word of that statement. Right after it, the גמרא moves on to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Calamity, punishment, trouble
Is prepared, is waiting

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this line as the start of something new. It is the tail end of a statement from the page before.

phrases.english: A calamity awaits him.
phrases.notes: This finishes a statement from the previous page about a person who goes without suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the statement carried over from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Such a person should know that trouble is waiting for him.

steps.title: Even the אבות could not stand up to strict judgment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר הגדול teaches that if הקב"ה judged אברהם, יצחק and יעקב strictly, they could not withstand His rebuke. He proves this from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: If הקב"ה had come into judgment with אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, they could not have stood up to the rebuke. As the פסוק says: "Now stand still, so I may plead with you before ה׳ about all the righteous acts of ה׳ that He did to you and to your fathers."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new statement about rebuke. Even our greatest ancestors could not survive being judged strictly by הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word צדקות in the פסוק. It says that what ה׳ did for the fathers was "righteous acts," meaning kindness, not what strict justice would have given them. If even the אבות needed kindness, nobody can claim to deserve good things on strict judgment alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Came into judgment, judged strictly
Rebuke
Righteous acts, here meaning acts of kindness
Stand still, stand ready

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that every good thing a person receives, even a great צדיק, comes from הקב"ה's kindness.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
Were the Holy One, Blessed be He, to come
into judgment with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,
they would not be able to stand before the rebuke,
as it is stated: "Now therefore stand still,"
"that I may plead with you before the Lord"
"concerning all the righteous acts of the Lord"
"which He did to you and to your fathers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about rebuke and judgment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the אבות survived only through הקב"ה's kindness, not through strict judgment.

steps.title: Does the generation follow the leader, or the leader the generation?
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק "זה דור דורשיו", רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבנן argue. One says the generation follows its leader, and the other says the leader follows his generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, Jacob, Selah." רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבנן disagree about this. One says: the generation follows its leader. The other says: the leader follows his generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק that links a generation with the people who lead it. It then brings a מחלוקת about which one depends on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a generation and its leader match each other. They argue about which way the influence goes. One view says the leader sets the tone for the people. The other says the people determine what kind of leader they get.

keyTerms.meaning: Generation
Those who seek Him, understood here as the leaders
Communal leader
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which opinion belongs to רבי יהודה נשיאה and which to רבנן. It just says "one says... and one says..."

phrases.english: "This is the generation of them that seek after Him,"
"that seek Your face, Jacob. Selah."

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia and the Rabbis disagree about it.
One says: the generation follows the leader,
and one says: the leader follows his generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת over whether the generation follows its leader or the leader follows his generation.

steps.title: What is the practical point of this dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the two sides are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to what matter is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this מחלוקת actually means in practice. This sets up the next step, where it tries out a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "generation follows the leader" is vague. It is not clear in what way one follows the other. The גמרא wants the exact point of the argument pinned down.

keyTerms.meaning: For what matter? What is the practical point?

phrases.english: With regard to what matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the מחלוקת in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way does one side "follow" the other?

steps.title: A first suggestion: the dispute is about goodness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument is about who makes whom good. One side says a good generation produces a good leader, and the other says a good leader produces a good generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it is about goodness: one Sage holds that if the generation is good, the leader is good. The other Sage holds that if the leader is good, the generation is good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out one possible answer to its question. The word אילימא, "if we say," warns us this answer is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, each view is a rule that goodness passes from one to the other. One view says it passes from the people to the leader. The other says it passes from the leader to the people. Both versions predict that a leader and his generation will always match in goodness.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say (a suggestion that will be challenged)
Goodness, being of good quality
One master holds
Generation (Aramaic)

phrases.english: If we say it is about goodness,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: אִי מְעַלֵּי דָּרָא מְעַלֵּי פַּרְנָס,
phrases.english: that one Sage holds: if the generation is good, the leader is good,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אִי מְעַלֵּי פַּרְנָס מְעַלֵּי דָּרָא
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: if the leader is good, the generation is good

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether a good generation brings a good leader or a good leader brings a good generation.

steps.title: צדקיה and יהויקים disprove that suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from history. צדקיה was good but his generation was not. יהויקים was not good but his generation was.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is צדקיה, who was good, and his generation was not good. And there is יהויקים, who was not good, and his generation was good!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from the previous step by pointing to two kings from תנ"ך. In both cases the king and his generation did not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If goodness always passed from leader to generation, or from generation to leader, they would always match. צדקיה breaks the rule in one direction, and יהויקים breaks it in the other. So both sides of the suggested argument are disproved by real history.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is (introducing a counterexample)
צדקיה, the last king of יהודה
יהויקים, an earlier king of יהודה

phrases.english: — but there is Zedekiah,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה מְעַלֵּי וְדָרֵיהּ לָא הֲוָה מְעַלֵּי,
phrases.english: who was good, and his generation was not good,
and there is Jehoiakim, who was not good,
and his generation was good!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיכָּא צִדְקִיָּה, דַּהֲוָה מְעַלֵּי וְדָרֵיהּ לָא הֲוָה מְעַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested explanation in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the dispute is about goodness passing between a leader and his generation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Historical counterexamples show a good king with a bad generation and a bad king with a good generation. So neither direction of the suggested rule holds true.
steps.whatToRemember: The simple reading, that goodness passes between leader and generation, is challenged by צדקיה and יהויקים. The גמרא will need another explanation of the מחלוקת.

steps.title: Proof that יהויקים and צדקיה did not match their generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains the word בראשית in the פסוק about יהויקים. הקב"ה wanted to return the world to תהו ובהו because of יהויקים, but his good generation calmed Him. He wanted to do the same because of צדקיה's bad generation, but righteous צדקיה calmed Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What does the פסוק mean, "In the beginning of the reign of יהויקים king of Judah"? הקב"ה wanted to return the world to emptiness and chaos because of יהויקים. Once He looked at his generation, He calmed down. הקב"ה wanted to return the world to emptiness and chaos because of צדקיה's generation. Once He looked at צדקיה, He calmed down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the facts it used in its challenge. It shows that יהויקים was wicked while his generation was good, and that צדקיה was good while his generation was wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בראשית reminds us of the beginning of Creation, before there was anything but תהו ובהו. Both kings show the leader and the generation on opposite levels. That breaks the idea from step 5 that goodness passes from one to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: In the beginning; here it hints back to the start of Creation
Emptiness and chaos, how the world was before Creation
His mind was settled; He calmed down and held back
His generation; the people living in a leader's time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kings. יהויקים was the wicked king with a good generation. צדקיה was the righteous king with a wicked generation.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah"?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 26:1. The word בראשית reminds us of the very start of the world.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to return the world to emptiness and chaos
phrases.notes: That means back to how it was before Creation, בראשית 1:2.

phrases.english: because of Jehoiakim.
Once He looked at his generation,
His mind was settled.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to return the world to emptiness and chaos
because of the generation of Zedekiah.
Once He looked at Zedekiah,
His mind was settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the historical facts used in the challenge of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 6 that יהויקים was wicked with a good generation and צדקיה was righteous with a wicked generation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explaining בראשית in ירמיהו 26:1.

steps.title: The argument is about harshness and gentleness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the idea that the argument is about goodness. It says the argument is about harshness and gentleness. A harsh leader goes with a harsh generation, and a gentle leader goes with a gentle generation, and the two sides argue about which one shapes the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are speaking about harshness and gentleness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what the argument is about. It is not about good and bad, but about harsh and gentle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from יהויקים and צדקיה only showed that righteousness does not pass between leader and generation. Personality and style, harsh or gentle, can still match. So רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבנן argue only about who shapes whose style.

keyTerms.meaning: Harshness, strictness, toughness
Gentleness, calmness, softness
Rather; drops the earlier idea and gives a new one

steps.whatToRemember: A leader and his generation can be on different levels of righteousness. They do match in their style, harsh or gentle. The only argument is whether the leader shapes the generation or the generation shapes the leader.

phrases.english: Rather, regarding harshness and gentleness
we are speaking.
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: the argument in step 3 about "זה דור דורשיו" was really about this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 6 and 7 by changing what the argument is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes what the argument is about, from goodness to style.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about whether a righteous leader makes a righteous generation, or the other way around.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about harshness and gentleness. Each side holds that one of them, leader or generation, shapes the other's style.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק יש בערכין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the end of the third פרק of ערכין, called יש בערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יש בערכין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It closes פרק יש בערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new teaching is added here. It marks the end of the פרק and shows our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a פרק
The name of this פרק, taken from its first words

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"There are in valuations" (the name of the chapter).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer of step 8.

steps.title: Four rules that open the new chapter
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists four rules: affordability follows the one who vows, age follows the person pledged, the amount follows the person being valued, and the valuation is fixed at the time of the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How much a person can afford goes by the one who vows. The age goes by the one whose value was pledged. The ערך amount goes by the person being valued. And the ערך is set by the time it was made.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק starts with a משנה that lists four basic rules about ערכין. This sets up the explanations that come right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule tells us whose details count. Money comes from the vower's pocket, so his wealth matters. The person being valued decides the age and the amount, measured on the day of the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא will discuss
Affordability, literally 'what the hand can reach'
The one who makes the vow and has to pay
The person whose ערך is being given
The time when the ערך vow was made

steps.whyThisMatters: These four rules are the frame for the whole פרק, which is named after its first words, השג יד.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Affordability goes by the one who vows,
and the years go by the one vowed about,
and the valuations go by the one being valued,
and the valuation goes by the time of the valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן closing פרק יש בערכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Affordability follows the vower. Age and the ערך amount follow the person valued, as of the time of the vow.

steps.title: Explaining that affordability follows the one who vows
steps.stepSummary: A poor person who gives a rich person's ערך pays a poor person's amount. A rich person who gives a poor person's ערך pays the full rich amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does affordability follow the vower? A poor person who pledged a rich person's ערך gives a poor person's ערך. A rich person who pledged a poor person's ערך gives a rich person's ערך.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its first rule with two examples. The wealth of the one who vows decides how much is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rich or poor status of the person being valued does not matter. Only the payer's ability to pay counts. A poor payer gets the reduced amount, and a rich payer owes the full fixed sum.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? This opens an explanation of the rule
A poor person's ערך, the lower amount based on what he can afford
A rich person's ערך, the full sum the תורה sets
Pledged someone's ערך

phrases.english: Affordability goes by the one who vows — how so?
A poor person who valuated a rich person
gives a poor person's valuation,
and a rich person who valuated a poor person
gives a rich person's valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the four rules from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ערכין, the payer's wealth decides the amount, not the wealth of the person being valued.

steps.title: Offerings work the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: If someone pledges a מצורע's offerings, he brings a poor or rich offering based on the מצורע's wealth, not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with קרבנות it is not so. If someone said, 'The offering of this מצורע is on me,' then if the מצורע is poor, he brings a poor person's offering. If the מצורע is rich, he brings a rich person's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts ערכין with קרבנות. With the offerings of a מצורע, the wealth of the person who needs the offering decides what is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the payer's wealth counted. Here the opposite happens: the pledger simply takes on the מצורע's own obligation, so the מצורע's status decides. This sets up רבי's argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought in the בית המקדש
A person with צרעת who brings offerings when he becomes pure
The smaller offering a poor מצורע brings
'Upon me', meaning I take this obligation on myself

phrases.english: But with offerings it is not so,
for if one said:
"The offering of this leper is upon me,"
if the leper was poor,
he brings a poor person's offering;
if rich, he brings a rich person's offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the ערכין rule from step 11 with the rule for קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone pledges a מצורע's offerings, the type of offering follows the מצורע's wealth.

steps.title: רבי says ערכין can work like the offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that the poor vower pays little only because the rich person owed nothing. If a poor person takes on a rich person's existing ערך, he pays the rich amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I say that even with ערכין it is like this. Why does a poor person who pledged a rich person's ערך pay a poor amount? Because the rich person owes nothing. But if a rich person said, 'My ערך is on me,' and a poor person heard and said, 'What he said is on me,' the poor person pays a rich person's ערך.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with how sharply the משנה split ערכין from קרבנות. He shows a ערכין case that works just like the מצורע case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether a debt already exists. In the plain case the poor person creates a brand-new debt, so his own wealth counts. When the rich man has already taken on his own ערך, the poor man is taking on that existing rich debt, just as in the מצורע case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I say', introducing the sage's own view
'My ערך is upon me', pledging one's own value
'What this one said is upon me', taking on someone else's pledge
Obligated, owing

steps.whatToRemember: In ערכין, the payer's wealth normally decides. רבי adds that if the poor person takes on a debt the rich person already has, he pays the rich amount, as with a מצורע's offerings.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying a poor person who simply pledges a rich person's ערך pays the rich amount. He agrees that case pays a poor amount. He is only talking about joining an obligation the rich man already took on.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: I say:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: even with valuations it is so,
for why is it

phrases.aramaic: עָנִי שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָשִׁיר נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָנִי,
phrases.english: that a poor person who valuated a rich person gives a poor person's valuation?
Because the rich person owes nothing.
But a rich person who said: "My valuation is upon me,"
and a poor person heard and said:
"What this one said is upon me" —
phrases.notes: Here the rich man already owes his own ערך, so the poor man is taking on that same debt.

phrases.english: gives a rich person's valuation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי: אַף בָּעֲרָכִין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the full contrast between ערכין and קרבנות drawn in step 12, using the reasoning behind step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person who takes on a rich person's existing ערך obligation pays a rich person's ערך.

steps.title: Shouldn't the משנה say 'the one who values'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording: affordability should be tied to the מעריך (valuer), not the נודר (vower).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Affordability depends on the one who values!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning a word in the משנה. The משנה said affordability follows the נודר, but this whole פרק is about ערכין, so it should have said מעריך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about valuations (ערכין), not ordinary vows (נדרים). So the expected word is מעריך, 'the one who values.' The גמרא wants to know why the משנה used the word for a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Affordability; literally 'what the hand can reach,' meaning what a person can afford to pay
The one who makes a valuation pledge (says 'my ערך' or 'so-and-so's ערך is on me')
The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Affordability depends on the one who values!
phrases.notes: The משנה said 'the one who vows.' The גמרא is asking why it didn't say 'the one who values.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The subject is ערכין, so the correct term should be מעריך, not נודר.

steps.title: The פסוק itself uses the word נודר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה used the word נודר because the פסוק about affordability uses that word.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'According to the means of him who vowed, so shall the כהן value him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting the פסוק. The תורה itself calls the valuer a נודר, so the משנה simply copied the תורה's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on ערכין in the תורה says 'אשר תשיג יד הנודר.' So the word נודר is not a mistake. It comes straight from the פסוק that is the source of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
The one who vows; here the תורה uses it for the one pledging a ערך
The כהן shall value him

phrases.english: As it is written:
"According to the means of him who vowed,
so shall the priest value him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural wording explains the משנה's language
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה used the wrong term for a valuation case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the פסוק's own word, נודר.

steps.title: Shouldn't the משנה say 'the one being valued'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges a second word: age should follow the נערך (person valued), not the נידר (subject of a vow).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The years follow the נידר'? It should be the נערך!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions a second word in the משנה. The age rule should be described with the word for 'the person being valued,' not 'the subject of a vow.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time there is no פסוק that uses the word נידר. So the earlier answer from the פסוק does not help here. The גמרא needs a new explanation for this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The years, meaning the age that sets the amount of the ערך
The subject of a vow; the person a vow is made about
The person being valued

phrases.english: The years follow the subject of the vow?
They follow the one being valued!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel wording challenge, this time on the second clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Age is a feature of the person being valued, so the term should be נערך.

steps.title: Same wording for consistency
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה already said נודר in the first clause, it used the matching word נידר in the second clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it said 'affordability follows the נודר,' it also said 'the years follow the נידר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה chose נידר only to match its first clause. The first clause used vow language, so the second one does too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a style answer called איידי, meaning 'since.' The word נידר is not meant to teach anything new. It just keeps the two clauses worded the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; used to explain that a word was chosen to match nearby wording
Also

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is now talking about regular נדרים. It is still about ערכין. Only the wording was borrowed.

phrases.english: Since it said "affordability follows the one who vows,"
it also said "the years follow the subject of the vow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נידר is the wrong term for the person valued.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה kept parallel wording with its first clause.

steps.title: Why does a poor vower pay the poor amount?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's example of a poor person valuing a rich person and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does affordability follow the vower? A poor person who values a rich person gives a poor person's ערך. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule again, this time to ask for its source. It wants to know why the vower's wealth counts and not the wealth of the person being valued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but not the reason. The גמרא asks מאי טעמא to find the source for tying affordability to the vower.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person's ערך: a reduced amount based on what he can afford
What is the reason?
How so? (introduces an example)

phrases.english: Affordability follows the one who vows; how so?
A poor person who valued a rich person
gives a poor person's valuation.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wording to the source of the rule quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for basing affordability on the vower.

steps.title: The תורה ties it to the vower
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'according to the means of him who vowed' shows that the תורה made affordability depend on the vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says 'according to the means of him who vowed': the תורה made it depend on the vower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the same פסוק as before. The פסוק speaks about the means of the one who vowed, so his wealth is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יד הנודר' point to the person who made the pledge. They do not point to the person whose ערך is being given. So a poor vower pays according to his own poverty.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the פסוק says
The תורה (literally 'the Merciful One') made it depend on

steps.whatToRemember: In ערכין, how much a person can afford is measured by the one who made the pledge, based on 'יד הנודר.'

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"According to the means of him who vowed" —
the Merciful One made it depend on the one who vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's phrase 'יד הנודר' ties affordability to the vower.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on a מצורע's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: with offerings it is different. If one pledges a poor מצורע's offering, he brings a poor man's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with offerings it is not so. If someone said 'this מצורע's offering is on me,' and the מצורע was poor, he brings a poor man's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case about a מצורע's offerings. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With offerings, the law follows the מצורע's wealth and not the wealth of the person who pledged. The גמרא repeats this line so it can question it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought in the בית המקדש
A person with צרעת who brings offerings when he becomes טהור
The cheaper offering the תורה allows a poor מצורע to bring

phrases.english: But with offerings it is not so,
for example, one who said:
"The offering of this מצורע is upon me,"
if the מצורע was poor,
he brings a poor person's offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the next clause of the משנה (step 12) to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pledged מצורע offering follows the מצורע's wealth.

steps.title: But the vower is rich, not poor!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a rich vower can bring a poor offering, since the תורה says the cheap offering is for 'if he is poor.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if the one who pledged is rich? But the תורה said 'and if he is poor,' and this vower is not poor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling. The תורה allows the cheap offering only for someone poor, and here the person paying is rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ואם דל הוא' makes the cheap offering depend on being poor. If the person paying for the offering is rich, it seems he should not get the poor man's discount, even though the מצורע himself is poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes the vow on his behalf
'And if he is poor' — the פסוק allowing the cheaper offering
And even though

phrases.english: Even though the one vowing for him is rich?
The Merciful One said "and if he is poor,"
and this one is not poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a pledged poor מצורע's offering is a poor offering even if the vower is rich
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits the cheap offering to someone who is poor, and the rich vower does not fit.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the vower was also poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that the משנה's case is where the one who pledged the offering is himself poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: the משנה is talking about a case where the one who made the vow is also poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. The cheap offering is brought because the vower is poor too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a rich vower cannot use the poor man's offering, since the פסוק says 'if he is poor.' רבי יצחק narrows the case so the vower is poor as well. Now nobody in the case is rich, so the cheap offering fits.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who vowed for him (here, the person who pledged the מצורע's offering)
Poor

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
When the one who vowed for him was poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כְּשֶׁהָיָה מַדִּירוֹ עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the vower is also poor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say even a rich vower brings the poor offering, which goes against 'if he is poor.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is speaking only where the vower is also poor.

steps.title: Maybe the תורה's leniency is only for the מצורע himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק says 'הוא', so maybe the cheap offering is allowed only when the מצורע himself pays, not a vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the תורה showed mercy only to the מצורע himself. For the one who vowed for him, it did not, since it is written 'he.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק's answer. Even a poor vower should not get the cheap offering, because the פסוק seems to talk only about the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוא' (he) in the פסוק points to the מצורע himself. So the leniency of the poor man's offering may belong only to him. A different person who vowed to pay might not be included at all, even if he is poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the תורה) showed mercy / was lenient
'He', the word in the פסוק that seems to limit the leniency to the מצורע himself

phrases.english: But perhaps the Merciful One had mercy only on him himself,
phrases.notes: 'Him himself' means the poor מצורע who is bringing the offering.

phrases.english: but on the one who vowed for him, not,
for it is written: 'he.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21: 'ואם דל הוא' — 'and if he is poor.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's answer from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that a poor vower may bring the poor offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'הוא' limits the leniency to the מצורע himself, so a vower, even a poor one, should not be included.

steps.title: 'His means do not suffice' includes the vower
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the extra words 'ואין ידו משגת' come to include the poor vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: the words 'and his means do not suffice' come to include the one who vowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק. Another phrase in the same פסוק adds the vower to the leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'if he is poor.' The extra words 'and his means do not suffice' teach something new: anyone whose means fall short, including a poor vower. So 'הוא' does not shut the vower out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And his means do not suffice', a phrase in the פסוק about the poor מצורע
To include (a phrase in the פסוק brings in an extra case)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
'And his means do not suffice'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21, the same פסוק, right after 'if he is poor.'

phrases.english: comes to include the one who vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וְאֵין יָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַנּוֹדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 with a different phrase in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Drawing on an extra phrase in the פסוק to include another case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הוא' limits the poor offering to the מצורע himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ואין ידו משגת' includes a poor vower as well.

steps.title: Then what does 'with offerings it is not so' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק: if the vower's wealth decides, a rich vower would bring a rich offering, and the משנה's contrast between ערכין and offerings would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the one who vowed is rich, does he then bring the rich offering? If so, what does the משנה mean by 'but with offerings it is not so'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רבי יצחק's answer from the wording of the משנה itself. His approach would make offerings work just like ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יצחק's logic, the vower's means decide, so a rich vower brings a rich offering. But that is exactly the rule for ערכין, where the vower's means decide. The משנה says offerings are different, which suggests the מצורע's means decide even when the vower is rich.

keyTerms.meaning: Rich
In the manner of wealth, meaning the rich man's offering
It is not so, the משנה's contrast between offerings and ערכין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In ערכין the vower's wealth decides. The משנה says offerings are different, so there the מצורע's wealth should decide. That is why רבי יצחק's answer is in trouble.

phrases.english: But if the one who vowed for him is rich,
does he then indeed bring the offering of a rich person?
If so, what is the meaning of
'but with offerings it is not so'?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 12, which set offerings apart from ערכין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מַדִּירוֹ עָשִׁיר, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמַיְיתֵי בַּעֲשִׁירוּת? אִם כֵּן, מַאי אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יצחק's answer is defended, the גמרא challenges it from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's answer that the vower's poverty is what allows the poor offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the vower's means decide, then a rich vower brings a rich offering, just like ערכין. Then the משנה's words 'with offerings it is not so' would have nothing to contrast.
